gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Noto Sans Nushu reads modern and tall, its terminals pulled well away from the stroke body. Noto Sans Nushu takes the quiet seat while College, a plain sans partner's loud display opposite, carries the swagger.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Noto Sans Ogham stands its lowercase tall enough to look bold, with wide gaps in the e that keep each word legible. College adds a glassy, neon-tube thickness.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: College comes in with straight-edged, constant strokes and big counters, all authority. Noto Sans Ol Chiki holds its curve tails back and packs words into solid blocks, which is where it does its best work.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-old-hung: College draws its rounds and stems in a single weight, so it looks dynamic and commanding. And Noto Sans Old Hungarian keeps its wide apertures open even tiny, which makes shrinking the heading the one move to avoid.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-old-ital: Noto Sans Old Italic is a sans-serif with hardly any gap between x-height and cap height, and its curve endings stay apart. And College, with rounds and stems in one weight, handles the loud display work while the body does the steady talking.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-old-nort: Noto Sans Old North Arabian sets a dense, tall lowercase band. College, with a stroke like a stylus held at fixed pressure, earns its keep when it is big and short, with outward-pointing tongs in the body underneath.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-old-perm: A technical drafting pen seems to have drawn College, authoritative and unwavering in every curve. Noto Sans Old Permic is friendlier beside it, a plain sans with rounded forms open to the side and lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-old-pers: Lofty and light. Noto Sans Old Persian lets its open counters breathe into the white space, a plain sans body, and College, with the weight of a drawn wire, keeps any longer stretch feeling clear and crisp.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-old-sogd: Noto Sans Old Sogdian reads crisp and tall, its x-height nearly touching cap height and its wide-mouthed letters holding up when shrunk. College keeps one line width through curves and straights for the headline punch.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-old-turk: Noto Sans Old Turkic brings chunky, tall lowercase with open-mouthed curves that stay clear. And College, its strokes built like pipes, takes the display role above while the sans-serif body fills in below.
